From: Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@orionpayments.com>

Date: 2027-05-06T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: DPA & subprocessors for Dedicated vs Private/VPC deployment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Orion is moving fast and we need the legal/data hygiene check before we commit to a Dedicated cluster. Two asks to kick off the DPA discussion:

1) Can you share a subprocessor matrix that distinguishes which subprocessors are involved for Hosted, Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pools), and Private/VPC (customer-managed networking)? Specifically we need to understand: encryption key access, where customer data rests for each deployment mode, and whether any cross-border transfers occur.

2) We prefer DocuSign for execution. Can you provision a signature-ready DPA or tell me the typical timeline for redlines? Procurement is available at procurement@orionpayments.com.

Attachments: sample_req_form.pdf (procurement)

Thanks,
Jordan Lowe
Head of Platform Security
Orion Payments

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-05-06T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA & subprocessors for Dedicated vs Private/VPC deployment

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Rafael (legal) and Mina (privacy/compliance). Quick plan below, and I attached an initial redline to speed things along.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- Today: we share the subprocessor matrix by deployment and a redline of our standard DPA (attached: Orion_DPA_redline_v1.docx).
- Tue (2 business days): Rafael to confirm any legal exceptions for customer-controlled keying / on-prem language.
- Thu: finalize technical annex (data flow map + storage locations) and prepare DocuSign envelope.

High-level clarifications up front:
- Private/on-prem deployment: Redwood does not engage cloud subprocessors for model serving inside a customer-controlled air-gapped installation. Where customers manage the infrastructure and keys, Redwood’s role is limited to the control plane (if requested) — we can carve that out in the DPA.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved capacity): GPUs are in our cloud pools; we use a limited set of subprocessors (listed in the matrix) for telemetry, monitoring, and infra. For customers requiring no cross-border transfers, we can pin region and add a data locality clause.

I attached a CSV that maps subprocessors to deployment types and notes SOC2 coverage. Rafael — see comments in the redline about KMS options and the suggested addendum for Customer-Controlled Keying (CCK).

Kimberly Park
Head, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

On Thu, May 6, 2027 at 10:21 AM kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
> Jordan — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Rafael (legal) and Mina (privacy/compliance). Quick plan below, and I attached an initial redline to speed things along.

Thanks — I reviewed Orion_DPA_redline_v1.docx and added tracked comments. Two legal points to call out here:

1) Customer-Controlled Keying (CCK) — For Dedicated we can offer two options: Redwood-managed KMS with contractual controls (standard), or CCK with an addendum that limits Redwood’s ability to decrypt customer data and removes subprocessors from key access. The CCK addendum should state expressly that logging and telemetry will be metadata-only unless customer authorizes access.

2) Subprocessor notification window — proposal: 30 days for new subprocessors for Dedicated; none required for Private/on-prem because no Redwood-managed subprocessors touch data in that configuration.

Jordan: I noted one of your requested subprocessors (CloudOps monitoring partner) as "region-limited" in the CSV — Alex Torres from CloudOps is cc'd to confirm they can operate exclusively in the AWS us-east-2 region if required.

I also proposed a small data transfer clause that allows execution of standard SCCs for EU->US transfers and a fallback to controller-to-controller transfer mechanisms for enterprise customers who require them.

If these are acceptable, I'll prepare a clean version for DocuSign and append the CCK addendum for your review.

— Rafael Mendes
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — that layout helps. A couple of quick responses: 

- CCK is a hard requirement for our production card-data lanes; we'll need the addendum and the explicit prohibition on Redwood personnel accessing keys without written authorization.
- For the subprocessor notification window: 30 days is fine. Procurement would like SOC2 evidence for the named subprocessors (monitoring, telemetry, backup). Can you point us to recent reports or an SOC2 letter?

Procurement contact is on copy. We're aiming to sign by EOD Friday next week, so appreciate the DocuSign-ready version.

Jordan Lowe
Head of Platform Security — Orion Payments
